case_title: Shiva Kumar @ Shiva @ Shivamurthy v. State of Karnataka
previous_criminal_record: No. First offence; the appellant's counsel also submitted he has no antecedents
evidence_type: Recovery (body at accused's instance; clothing and footwear near body); complaint by maternal uncle reporting victim missing
aggravating_circumstances: Brutal manner of killing after rape; victim was a woman working late-night shifts; the facts shock the conscience
mitigating_circumstances: Accused aged 27 at conviction; wife, small child and aged parents; first offence; no antecedents (noted as not decisive by itself); satisfactory jail conduct and BA completed in jail (per counsel)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.366, 376 and 302 IPC; rigorous life imprisonment for the rest of life (no release)
high_court_outcome: Appellant's appeal against conviction and sentence dismissed; State's enhancement appeal dismissed
offence_finally_established: IPC s.366 (kidnapping/abduction for the purpose stated in s.366), s.376 (rape), s.302 (murder)
neutral_facts: The victim, a woman employed by a company with an office in Electronic City, Bengaluru, often had to work late into the night or early morning. The company provided employees with cars on designated routes. At about 2:00 a.m., the victim left the office intending to take the company vehicle on route no. 131. The accused, who was the driver of a company vehicle, told the victim that the route 131 vehicle was not available and that she would have to travel in his vehicle on route no. 405. The victim got into the car driven by the accused. The victim's maternal uncle lodged a complaint stating that the victim was missing. The victim's dead body was later recovered at the instance of the accused. The victim's clothes and footwear were found near the body. The victim was 28 years old when her life was cut short in a brutal manner. The prosecution case was that the accused committed rape and murder of the victim after taking her in his vehicle.
offence_severity: Maximum: death penalty (judgment refers to an offence punishable with death penalty; alternative life imprisonment). Minimum: not stated
physical_harm: Death of victim after rape; injuries not described
key_evidence_accepted: Prosecution proof of rape (s.376) and kidnapping/abduction (s.366); recovery of body at accused's instance; recovery of clothing and footwear near body
custody_duration: Approximately 17 years and 2 months (as submitted by appellant's counsel)
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 31.05.2016; Supreme Court: 28.03.2023
legal_representation: Accused: K. Parameshwar, Shekhar G Devasa and others (M/s. Devasa & Co.). State: Shubhranshu Padhi, Vishal Banshal and others
investigation_status: Complaint lodged by maternal uncle; body recovered at accused's instance; charge sheet and FIR details not stated
procedural_irregularity: Trial Court could not have directed that the appellant not be released for the rest of his life
appeal_history: Trial court: rigorous life imprisonment for rest of life. High Court: both appeals dismissed. Supreme Court: sentence modified to 30 years' actual imprisonment before release
prosecution_argument: Constitutional Courts can impose modified sentences even where death penalty is not imposed; the most stringent punishment was contemplated and the High Court reiterated the Trial Court's view
defence_argument: Modified sentence can be imposed only by Constitutional Courts and only when commuting death penalty; Sessions Court could not impose it; relied on Sriharan and Swamy Shraddananda
legal_principle_applied: Constitutional Courts (High Court and Supreme Court) may impose a fixed-term or modified life sentence of more than 14 years even where death penalty is not imposed; fixed term cannot be below 14 years per s.433A Cr.P.C.
precedent_relied_upon: Union of India v. V. Sriharan (2016) 7 SCC 1 (followed); Swamy Shraddananda (2) (2008) 13 SCC 767, Sahib Hussain (2013) 9 SCC 778, Gurvail Singh (2013) 10 SCC 631 (referred to)
sentencing_rationale: Brutal case; High Court balanced aggravating and mitigating circumstances; undue leniency would harm public confidence; victim's rights considered; fixed 30-year term imposed
judicial_mitigating_factors: Age 27 at conviction; wife, small child and aged parents (as noted by Trial Court); first offence; possibility of reformation considered
judicial_aggravating_factors: Brutal manner of the crime; need to avoid undue leniency in a brutal case; rights of the victim; safety of women working at night
other_sentence_order: Life imprisonment with release only after 30 years of actual sentence; no remission before that period
